title: oku page v2
description: Compact authoring shape. A page is { k:'page', t, m?, b }. The b array carries markdown strings interleaved with typed primitive objects. Sections are implicit from heading levels inside markdown.

t.description: Document title — drives <title> and the cover h1.

b.description: Sequence of blocks. A string is parsed as GFM markdown. An object is a typed primitive.

meta.description: Page-level metadata. accent picks the page color token; the rest are surfaced in cover, nav tooltips, and llms.txt.

accent.description: Kit color token (teal/amber/indigo/rose/violet/green/slate) or any CSS color.

block.description: A string (parsed as GFM markdown) or a typed primitive object.

image.description: Raster/vector image as a figure. src is a self-contained data: URI (preferred — keeps the doc offline) or a URL/path. Renders

width.description: Max width — number (px) or CSS length.

svg.description: Inline, author-authored SVG illustration (theme-aware via currentColor / CSS vars, scales with viewBox). Renders <figure> with the SVG inline. Scripts are stripped.

code.description: Annotated / multi-feature code block. Plain code should use a markdown fenced block inside a string in b[] instead.

src.description: Code body. Use (1), (2)… markers or external line/match specs in annotations.

content.description: HTML snippet (allow-list: code, strong, em, a).

ordered.description: true (default): numbered single-column flow. false: an unordered 2-up grid of link cards (navigation / parallel options) — no numerals, which would imply a sequence that isn't there.

href.description: When set, the step card wraps in an anchor to this target.

timeline.description: An ordered sequence of events on a vertical rail, each carrying a status. Use it when the ORDER and the STATE of each entry are both part of the point — a debugging story where a claim is later corrected, a decision log, an incident sequence. A step-flow is the neighbouring shape and answers a different question: it is a procedure the reader is meant to follow, so every step is equally true. Nothing here is a procedure.

label.description: Small chip before the title: the reader's own word for this entry ("claim #1", "corrected", "2026-03-04", "v0.4.0"). The status carries the colour; this carries the meaning.

status.description: note (default): a plain event, quiet hollow dot. done: settled / verified / shipped — filled dot, success colour. open: claimed but not settled — hollow warning dot. dropped: retracted, superseded, abandoned — hollow danger dot.

compare-grid.description: N-card comparison grid. Card body is a markdown string.

preview.description: Show each card's linked figure as a silhouette under its title. Only cards whose href is an in-page anchor with a figure after it get one.

example.description: Code + rendered-result pair. Code on the left, output on the right.

table.description: Sortable / filterable / chippable table. Plain non-interactive tables should use markdown pipe-table syntax inside a string.

status.description: Map a cell value → verdict; matching cells in this column render as a coloured status pill. Locale-neutral: the author maps their own values, so the kit bakes in no English status words.

chart.description: Data-driven chart. type selects render mode; payload fields vary per type.

tree.description: treemap (flat array of leaves) OR sunburst (nested object with label/value/children).

chart-grid.description: Small multiples — same chart shape across N data panels.

info-tip.description: A <details> disclosure: a one-line summary the reader can expand. For the detail the curious minority wants without taxing everyone else.

content.description: Markdown strings and/or typed blocks, same as a page body.
